388	    def _validate_config(self):
389	        config = self.config
390	        # number of GPUs total
391	        n_gpus = config.trainer.n_gpus_per_node * config.trainer.nnodes
392	        if config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.strategy == "megatron":
393	            model_parallel_size = (
394	                config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.tensor_model_parallel_size
395	                * config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.pipeline_model_parallel_size
396	            )
397	            assert (
398	                n_gpus % (model_parallel_size * config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.context_parallel_size) == 0
399	            ), (
400	                f"n_gpus ({n_gpus}) must be divisible by model_parallel_size ({model_parallel_size}) times "
401	                f"context_parallel_size ({config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.context_parallel_size})"
402	            )
403	            megatron_dp = n_gpus // (
404	                model_parallel_size * config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.context_parallel_size
405	            )
406	            minimal_bsz = megatron_dp * config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu
407	        else:
408	            minimal_bsz = n_gpus
409	
410	        # 1. Check total batch size for data correctness
411	        real_train_batch_size = config.data.train_batch_size * config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n
412	        assert real_train_batch_size % minimal_bsz == 0, (
413	            f"real_train_batch_size ({real_train_batch_size}) must be divisible by minimal possible batch size "
414	            f"({minimal_bsz})"
415	        )
416	
417	        # A helper function to check "micro_batch_size" vs "micro_batch_size_per_gpu"
418	        # We throw an error if the user sets both. The new convention is "..._micro_batch_size_per_gpu".
419	        def check_mutually_exclusive(mbs, mbs_per_gpu, name: str):
420	            """Validate mutually exclusive micro batch size configuration options.
421	
422	            Ensures that users don't set both deprecated micro_batch_size and
423	            the new micro_batch_size_per_gpu parameters simultaneously.
424	
425	            Args:
426	                mbs: Deprecated micro batch size parameter value.
427	                mbs_per_gpu: New micro batch size per GPU parameter value.
428	                name (str): Configuration section name for error messages.
429	
430	            Raises:
431	                ValueError: If both parameters are set or neither is set.
432	            """
433	            settings = {
434	                "actor_rollout_ref.actor": "micro_batch_size",
435	                "critic": "micro_batch_size",
436	                "reward_model": "micro_batch_size",
437	                "actor_rollout_ref.ref": "log_prob_micro_batch_size",
438	                "actor_rollout_ref.rollout": "log_prob_micro_batch_size",
439	            }
440	
441	            if name in settings:
442	                param = settings[name]
443	                param_per_gpu = f"{param}_per_gpu"
444	
445	                if mbs is None and mbs_per_gpu is None:
446	                    raise ValueError(
447	                        f"[{name}] Please set at least one of '{name}.{param}' or '{name}.{param_per_gpu}'."
448	                    )
449	
450	                if mbs is not None and mbs_per_gpu is not None:
451	                    raise ValueError(
452	                        f"[{name}] You have set both '{name}.{param}' AND '{name}.{param_per_gpu}'. Please remove "
453	                        f"'{name}.{param}' because only '*_{param_per_gpu}' is supported (the former is deprecated)."
454	                    )
455	
456	        if not config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz:
457	            # actor: ppo_micro_batch_size vs. ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu
458	            check_mutually_exclusive(
459	                config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size,
460	                config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu,
461	                "actor_rollout_ref.actor",
462	            )
463	
464	            if self.use_reference_policy:
465	                # reference: log_prob_micro_batch_size vs. log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu
466	                check_mutually_exclusive(
467	                    config.actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_micro_batch_size,
468	                    config.actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu,
469	                    "actor_rollout_ref.ref",
470	                )
471	
472	            #  The rollout section also has log_prob_micro_batch_size vs. log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu
473	            check_mutually_exclusive(
474	                config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_micro_batch_size,
475	                config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu,
476	                "actor_rollout_ref.rollout",
477	            )
478	
479	        if self.use_critic and not config.critic.use_dynamic_bsz:
480	            # Check for critic micro-batch size conflicts
481	            check_mutually_exclusive(
482	                config.critic.ppo_micro_batch_size, config.critic.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu, "critic"
483	            )
484	
485	        # Check for reward model micro-batch size conflicts
486	        if config.reward_model.enable and not config.reward_model.use_dynamic_bsz:
487	            check_mutually_exclusive(
488	                config.reward_model.micro_batch_size, config.reward_model.micro_batch_size_per_gpu, "reward_model"
489	            )
490	
491	        # Actor
492	        # check if train_batch_size is larger than ppo_mini_batch_size
493	        # if NOT dynamic_bsz, we must ensure:
494	        #    ppo_mini_batch_size is divisible by ppo_micro_batch_size
495	        #    ppo_micro_batch_size * sequence_parallel_size >= n_gpus
496	        if not config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz:
497	            assert config.data.train_batch_size >= config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size
498	            sp_size = config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.get("ulysses_sequence_parallel_size", 1)
499	            if config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size is not None:
500	                assert (
501	                    config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size
502	                    % config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size
503	                    == 0
504	                )
505	                assert config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size * sp_size >= n_gpus
506	
507	        assert config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.loss_agg_mode in [
508	            "token-mean",
509	            "seq-mean-token-sum",
510	            "seq-mean-token-mean",
511	            "seq-mean-token-sum-norm",
512	        ], f"Invalid loss_agg_mode: {config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.loss_agg_mode}"
513	
514	        if self.config.algorithm.use_kl_in_reward and config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss:
515	            print("NOTICE: You have both enabled in-reward kl and kl loss.")
516	
517	        # critic
518	        if self.use_critic and not config.critic.use_dynamic_bsz:
519	            assert config.data.train_batch_size >= config.critic.ppo_mini_batch_size
520	            sp_size = config.critic.get("ulysses_sequence_parallel_size", 1)
521	            if config.critic.ppo_micro_batch_size is not None:
522	                assert config.critic.ppo_mini_batch_size % config.critic.ppo_micro_batch_size == 0
523	                assert config.critic.ppo_micro_batch_size * sp_size >= n_gpus
524	
525	        # Check if use_remove_padding is enabled when using sequence parallelism for fsdp
526	        if config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.strategy in {"fsdp", "fsdp2"} and (
527	            config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.get("ulysses_sequence_parallel_size", 1) > 1
528	            or config.actor_rollout_ref.ref.get("ulysses_sequence_parallel_size", 1) > 1
529	        ):
530	            assert config.actor_rollout_ref.model.use_remove_padding, (
531	                "When using sequence parallelism for actor/ref policy, you must enable `use_remove_padding`."
532	            )
533	
534	        if self.use_critic and config.critic.strategy in {"fsdp", "fsdp2"}:
535	            if config.critic.get("ulysses_sequence_parallel_size", 1) > 1:
536	                assert config.critic.model.use_remove_padding, (
537	                    "When using sequence parallelism for critic, you must enable `use_remove_padding`."
538	                )
539	
540	        if config.data.get("val_batch_size", None) is not None:
541	            print(
542	                "WARNING: val_batch_size is deprecated."
543	                + " Validation datasets are sent to inference engines as a whole batch,"
544	                + " which will schedule the memory themselves."
545	            )
546	
547	        # check eval config
548	        if config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.do_sample:
549	            assert config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.temperature > 0, (
550	                "validation gen temperature should be greater than 0 when enabling do_sample"
551	            )
552	
553	        print("[validate_config] All configuration checks passed successfully!")

656	    def _maybe_log_val_generations(self, inputs, outputs, scores):
657	        """Log a table of validation samples to the configured logger (wandb or swanlab)"""
658	
659	        generations_to_log = self.config.trainer.log_val_generations
660	
661	        if generations_to_log == 0:
662	            return
663	
664	        import numpy as np
665	
666	        # Create tuples of (input, output, score) and sort by input text
667	        samples = list(zip(inputs, outputs, scores, strict=True))
668	        samples.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])  # Sort by input text
669	
670	        # Use fixed random seed for deterministic shuffling
671	        rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
672	        rng.shuffle(samples)
673	
674	        # Take first N samples after shuffling
675	        samples = samples[:generations_to_log]
676	
677	        # Log to each configured logger
678	        self.validation_generations_logger.log(self.config.trainer.logger, samples, self.global_steps)

680	    def _validate(self):
681	        data_source_lst = []
682	        reward_extra_infos_dict: dict[str, list] = defaultdict(list)
683	
684	        # Lists to collect samples for the table
685	        sample_inputs = []
686	        sample_outputs = []
687	        sample_scores = []
688	        sample_turns = []
689	
690	        for test_data in self.val_dataloader:
691	            test_batch = DataProto.from_single_dict(test_data)
692	
693	            # repeat test batch
694	            test_batch = test_batch.repeat(
695	                repeat_times=self.config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.n, interleave=True
696	            )
697	
698	            # we only do validation on rule-based rm
699	            if self.config.reward_model.enable and test_batch[0].non_tensor_batch["reward_model"]["style"] == "model":
700	                return {}
701	
702	            # Store original inputs
703	            input_ids = test_batch.batch["input_ids"]
704	            # TODO: Can we keep special tokens except for padding tokens?
705	            input_texts = [self.tokenizer.decode(ids, skip_special_tokens=True) for ids in input_ids]
706	            sample_inputs.extend(input_texts)

711	                if key in test_batch.non_tensor_batch:
712	                    non_tensor_batch_keys_to_pop.append(key)
713	            test_gen_batch = test_batch.pop(
714	                batch_keys=batch_keys_to_pop,
715	                non_tensor_batch_keys=non_tensor_batch_keys_to_pop,
716	            )
717	
718	            test_gen_batch.meta_info = {

721	                "recompute_log_prob": False,

725	            }
726	            print(f"test_gen_batch meta info: {test_gen_batch.meta_info}")
727	
728	            # pad to be divisible by dp_size

730	                self.actor_rollout_wg.world_size
731	                if not self.async_rollout_mode
732	                else self.config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.agent.num_workers
733	            )

1009	        """Reorder the data on single controller such that each dp rank gets similar total tokens"""
1010	        attention_mask = batch.batch["attention_mask"]

1012	        global_seqlen_lst = batch.batch["attention_mask"].view(batch_size, -1).sum(-1).tolist()  # (train_batch_size,)
1013	        world_size = self.actor_rollout_wg.world_size
1014	        global_partition_lst = get_seqlen_balanced_partitions(
1015	            global_seqlen_lst, k_partitions=world_size, equal_size=True
1016	        )
1017	        # reorder based on index. The data will be automatically equally partitioned by dispatch function
1018	        global_idx = torch.tensor([j for partition in global_partition_lst for j in partition])
1019	        batch.reorder(global_idx)
1020	        global_balance_stats = log_seqlen_unbalance(
1021	            seqlen_list=global_seqlen_lst, partitions=global_partition_lst, prefix=logging_prefix
1022	        )

1025	    def _prepare_batch_for_rollout(self, batch: DataProto, repeat_times: int):

1027	            batch.non_tensor_batch["uid"] = np.array(
1028	                [str(uuid.uuid4()) for _ in range(len(batch.batch))], dtype=object
1029	            )
1030	        # repeat to align with repeated responses in rollout
1031	        batch = batch.repeat(repeat_times=repeat_times, interleave=True)
1032	
1033	        # pop those keys for generation
1034	        batch_keys_to_pop = ["input_ids", "attention_mask", "position_ids"]

1041	            non_tensor_batch_keys=non_tensor_batch_keys_to_pop,
1042	        )
1043	        # pass global_steps to trace
1044	        gen_batch.meta_info["global_steps"] = self.global_steps
1045	        gen_batch.non_tensor_batch["sampling_seed"] = np.arange(len(gen_batch), dtype=np.int64) + 42 + self.global_steps * 100000

1063	    def _compute_old_log_prob(self, compute_log_prob_fn: Callable, batch: DataProto):
1064	        old_log_prob = compute_log_prob_fn(batch)
1065	        entropys = old_log_prob.batch["entropys"]
1066	        response_masks = batch.batch["response_mask"]
1067	        loss_agg_mode = self.config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.loss_agg_mode
1068	        entropy_agg = agg_loss(loss_mat=entropys, loss_mask=response_masks, loss_agg_mode=loss_agg_mode)
1069	        old_log_prob_metrics = {"actor/entropy": entropy_agg.detach().item()}
1070	        old_log_prob.batch.pop("entropys")
1071	        batch = batch.union(old_log_prob)
1072	
1073	        if "rollout_log_probs" in batch.batch.keys():
1074	            rollout_old_log_probs = batch.batch["rollout_log_probs"]
1075	            actor_old_log_probs = batch.batch["old_log_probs"]
1076	            responses = batch.batch["responses"]
1077	            response_mask = batch.batch["response_mask"]
1078	
1079	            rollout_probs = torch.exp(rollout_old_log_probs)
1080	            actor_probs = torch.exp(actor_old_log_probs)
1081	            rollout_probs_diff = actor_probs - rollout_probs
1082	            rollout_probs_diff = torch.masked_select(rollout_probs_diff, response_mask.bool())
1083	            rollout_probs_diff_abs = torch.abs(rollout_probs_diff)
1084	            rollout_probs_diff_max = torch.max(rollout_probs_diff)
1085	            rollout_probs_diff_min = torch.min(rollout_probs_diff)
1086	            rollout_probs_diff_mean = torch.mean(rollout_probs_diff_abs)
1087	            rollout_probs_diff_std = torch.std(rollout_probs_diff_abs)
1088	            actor_log_probs_min = torch.min(actor_old_log_probs * response_mask)
1089	            rollout_log_probs_min = torch.min(rollout_old_log_probs * response_mask)
1090	
1091	            masked_diff = (actor_probs - rollout_probs) * response_mask
1092	            max_diff_idx = torch.argmax(masked_diff)
1093	            max_diff_response_id = responses.flatten()[max_diff_idx]
1094	            min_diff_idx = torch.argmin(masked_diff)
1095	            min_diff_response_id = responses.flatten()[min_diff_idx]
1096	            print(f"max_diff_response_id: {max_diff_response_id}, {masked_diff.flatten()[max_diff_idx]}")
1097	            print(f"min_diff_response_id: {min_diff_response_id}, {masked_diff.flatten()[min_diff_idx]}")
1098	            rollout_probs_diff_0 = (actor_probs - rollout_probs)[0].detach().cpu().numpy()
1099	            response_id_0 = responses[0].detach().cpu().numpy()
1100	            response_mask_0 = response_mask[0].detach().cpu().numpy()
1101	            first_rollout = []
1102	            for i in range(len(response_mask_0)):
1103	                if response_mask_0[i]:
1104	                    first_rollout.append((response_id_0[i], rollout_probs_diff_0[i]))
1105	            # print(f"The first rollout {first_rollout}")
1106	            old_log_prob_metrics.update(
1107	                {
1108	                    "training/rollout_probs_diff_max": rollout_probs_diff_max.detach().item(),
1109	                    "training/rollout_probs_diff_min": rollout_probs_diff_min.detach().item(),
1110	                    "training/rollout_probs_diff_mean": rollout_probs_diff_mean.detach().item(),
1111	                    "training/rollout_probs_diff_std": rollout_probs_diff_std.detach().item(),
1112	                    "training/actor_log_probs_min": actor_log_probs_min.detach().item(),
1113	                    "training/rollout_log_probs_min": rollout_log_probs_min.detach().item(),
1114	                }
1115	            )
1116	        from run_support import parity_metrics
1117	        old_log_prob_metrics.update(parity_metrics(batch, self.global_steps))
1118	        return batch, old_log_prob_metrics

14	"""
15	A unified tracking interface that supports logging data to different backend
16	"""
17	
18	import dataclasses
19	import os
20	from enum import Enum
21	from functools import partial
22	from pathlib import Path
23	from typing import Any
24	
25	
26	class Tracking:
27	    """A unified tracking interface for logging experiment data to multiple backends.
28	
29	    This class provides a centralized way to log experiment metrics, parameters, and artifacts
30	    to various tracking backends including WandB, MLflow, SwanLab, TensorBoard, and console.
31	
32	    Attributes:
33	        supported_backend: List of supported tracking backends.
34	        logger: Dictionary of initialized logger instances for each backend.
35	    """
36	
37	    supported_backend = ["wandb", "mlflow", "swanlab", "vemlp_wandb", "tensorboard", "console", "clearml"]
38	
39	    def __init__(self, project_name, experiment_name, default_backend: str | list[str] = "console", config=None):
40	        if isinstance(default_backend, str):
41	            default_backend = [default_backend]
42	        for backend in default_backend:
43	            if backend == "tracking":
44	                import warnings
45	
46	                warnings.warn("`tracking` logger is deprecated. use `wandb` instead.", DeprecationWarning, stacklevel=2)
47	            else:
48	                assert backend in self.supported_backend, f"{backend} is not supported"
49	
50	        self.logger = {}
51	
52	        if "tracking" in default_backend or "wandb" in default_backend:
53	            import wandb
54	
55	            settings = None
56	            if config and config["trainer"].get("wandb_proxy", None):
57	                settings = wandb.Settings(https_proxy=config["trainer"]["wandb_proxy"])
58	            wandb.init(project=project_name, name=experiment_name, config=config, settings=settings)
59	            self.logger["wandb"] = wandb
60	
61	        if "mlflow" in default_backend:
62	            import os
63	
64	            import mlflow
65	
66	            MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI = os.environ.get("MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI", "sqlite:////tmp/mlruns.db")
67	            mlflow.set_tracking_uri(MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI)
68	
69	            # Project_name is actually experiment_name in MLFlow
70	            # If experiment does not exist, will create a new experiment
71	            experiment = mlflow.set_experiment(project_name)
72	            mlflow.start_run(experiment_id=experiment.experiment_id, run_name=experiment_name)
73	            mlflow.log_params(_compute_mlflow_params_from_objects(config))
74	            self.logger["mlflow"] = _MlflowLoggingAdapter()
75	
76	        if "swanlab" in default_backend:
77	            import os
78	
79	            import swanlab
80	
81	            SWANLAB_API_KEY = os.environ.get("SWANLAB_API_KEY", None)
82	            SWANLAB_LOG_DIR = os.environ.get("SWANLAB_LOG_DIR", "swanlog")
83	            SWANLAB_MODE = os.environ.get("SWANLAB_MODE", "cloud")
84	            if SWANLAB_API_KEY:
85	                swanlab.login(SWANLAB_API_KEY)  # NOTE: previous login information will be overwritten
86	
87	            if config is None:
88	                config = {}  # make sure config is not None, otherwise **config will raise error
89	            swanlab.init(
90	                project=project_name,
91	                experiment_name=experiment_name,
92	                config={"FRAMEWORK": "verl", **config},
93	                logdir=SWANLAB_LOG_DIR,
94	                mode=SWANLAB_MODE,
95	            )
96	            self.logger["swanlab"] = swanlab
97	
98	        if "vemlp_wandb" in default_backend:
99	            import os
100	
101	            import volcengine_ml_platform
102	            from volcengine_ml_platform import wandb as vemlp_wandb
103	
104	            volcengine_ml_platform.init(
105	                ak=os.environ["VOLC_ACCESS_KEY_ID"],
106	                sk=os.environ["VOLC_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"],
107	                region=os.environ["MLP_TRACKING_REGION"],
108	            )
109	
110	            vemlp_wandb.init(
111	                project=project_name,
112	                name=experiment_name,
113	                config=config,
114	                sync_tensorboard=True,
115	            )
116	            self.logger["vemlp_wandb"] = vemlp_wandb
117	
118	        if "tensorboard" in default_backend:
119	            self.logger["tensorboard"] = _TensorboardAdapter(project_name, experiment_name)
120	
121	        if "console" in default_backend:
122	            from verl.utils.logger import LocalLogger
123	
124	            self.console_logger = LocalLogger(print_to_console=True)
125	            self.logger["console"] = self.console_logger
126	
127	        if "clearml" in default_backend:
128	            self.logger["clearml"] = ClearMLLogger(project_name, experiment_name, config)
129	
130	    def log(self, data, step, backend=None):
131	        from run_support import append_metrics
132	        append_metrics(data, step)
133	        for default_backend, logger_instance in self.logger.items():
134	            if backend is None or default_backend in backend:
135	                logger_instance.log(data=data, step=step)
136	
137	    def __del__(self):
138	        if "wandb" in self.logger:
139	            self.logger["wandb"].finish(exit_code=0)
140	        if "swanlab" in self.logger:
141	            self.logger["swanlab"].finish()
142	        if "vemlp_wandb" in self.logger:
143	            self.logger["vemlp_wandb"].finish(exit_code=0)
144	        if "tensorboard" in self.logger:
145	            self.logger["tensorboard"].finish()
146	
147	        if "clearnml" in self.logger:
148	            self.logger["clearnml"].finish()
149	
150	
151	class ClearMLLogger:
152	    def __init__(self, project_name: str, experiment_name: str, config):
153	        self.project_name = project_name
154	        self.experiment_name = experiment_name
155	
156	        import clearml
157	
158	        self._task: clearml.Task = clearml.Task.init(
159	            task_name=experiment_name,
160	            project_name=project_name,
161	            continue_last_task=True,
162	            output_uri=False,
163	        )
164	
165	        self._task.connect_configuration(config, name="Hyperparameters")
166	
167	    def _get_logger(self):
168	        return self._task.get_logger()
169	
170	    def log(self, data, step):
171	        import numpy as np
172	        import pandas as pd
173	
174	        # logs = self._rewrite_logs(data)
175	        logger = self._get_logger()
176	        for k, v in data.items():
177	            title, series = k.split("/", 1)
178	
179	            if isinstance(v, int | float | np.floating | np.integer):
180	                logger.report_scalar(
181	                    title=title,
182	                    series=series,
183	                    value=v,
184	                    iteration=step,
185	                )
186	            elif isinstance(v, pd.DataFrame):
187	                logger.report_table(
188	                    title=title,
189	                    series=series,
190	                    table_plot=v,
191	                    iteration=step,
192	                )
193	            else:
194	                logger.warning(
195	                    f'Trainer is attempting to log a value of "{v}" of type {type(v)} for key "{k}". This '
196	                    f"invocation of ClearML logger's function is incorrect so this attribute was dropped. "
197	                )
198	
199	    def finish(self):
200	        self._task.mark_completed()
201	
202	
203	class _TensorboardAdapter:
204	    def __init__(self, project_name, experiment_name):
205	        import os
206	
207	        from torch.utils.tensorboard import SummaryWriter
208	
209	        tensorboard_dir = os.environ.get("TENSORBOARD_DIR", f"tensorboard_log/{project_name}/{experiment_name}")
210	        os.makedirs(tensorboard_dir, exist_ok=True)
211	        print(f"Saving tensorboard log to {tensorboard_dir}.")
212	        self.writer = SummaryWriter(tensorboard_dir)
213	
214	    def log(self, data, step):
215	        for key in data:
216	            self.writer.add_scalar(key, data[key], step)
217	
218	    def finish(self):
219	        self.writer.close()
220	
221	
222	class _MlflowLoggingAdapter:
223	    def log(self, data, step):
224	        import mlflow
225	
226	        results = {k.replace("@", "_at_"): v for k, v in data.items()}
227	        mlflow.log_metrics(metrics=results, step=step)
228	
229	
230	def _compute_mlflow_params_from_objects(params) -> dict[str, Any]:
231	    if params is None:
232	        return {}
233	
234	    return _flatten_dict(_transform_params_to_json_serializable(params, convert_list_to_dict=True), sep="/")
235	
236	
237	def _transform_params_to_json_serializable(x, convert_list_to_dict: bool):
238	    _transform = partial(_transform_params_to_json_serializable, convert_list_to_dict=convert_list_to_dict)
239	
240	    if dataclasses.is_dataclass(x):
241	        return _transform(dataclasses.asdict(x))
242	    if isinstance(x, dict):
243	        return {k: _transform(v) for k, v in x.items()}
244	    if isinstance(x, list):
245	        if convert_list_to_dict:
246	            return {"list_len": len(x)} | {f"{i}": _transform(v) for i, v in enumerate(x)}
247	        else:
248	            return [_transform(v) for v in x]
249	    if isinstance(x, Path):
250	        return str(x)
251	    if isinstance(x, Enum):
252	        return x.value
253	
254	    return x
255	
256	
257	def _flatten_dict(raw: dict[str, Any], *, sep: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
258	    import pandas as pd
259	
260	    ans = pd.json_normalize(raw, sep=sep).to_dict(orient="records")[0]
261	    assert isinstance(ans, dict)
262	    return ans
263

265	@dataclasses.dataclass
266	class ValidationGenerationsLogger:

# NOTE(sgm): this implementation only consider outcome supervision, where the reward is a scalar.
@register_adv_est(AdvantageEstimator.GRPO)  # or simply: @register_adv_est("grpo")
def compute_grpo_outcome_advantage(
    token_level_rewards: torch.Tensor,
    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
    index: np.ndarray,
    epsilon: float = 1e-6,
    norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo: bool = True,
    config: Optional[AlgoConfig] = None,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """
    Compute advantage for GRPO, operating only on Outcome reward
    (with only one scalar reward for each response).

    Args:
        token_level_rewards: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape is (bs, response_length)
        response_mask: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape is (bs, response_length)
        index: `(np.ndarray)`
            index array for grouping
        epsilon: `(float)`
            small value to avoid division by zero
        norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo: `(bool)`
            whether to scale the GRPO advantage
        config: `(Optional[AlgoConfig])`
            algorithm configuration object

    Note:
        If norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo is True, the advantage is scaled by the std, as in the original GRPO.
        If False, the advantage is not scaled, as in Dr.GRPO (https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.20783).

    Returns:
        advantages: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape is (bs, response_length)
        Returns: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape is (bs, response_length)
    """
    scores = token_level_rewards.sum(dim=-1)

    id2score = defaultdict(list)
    id2mean = {}
    id2std = {}

    with torch.no_grad():
        bsz = scores.shape[0]
        for i in range(bsz):
            id2score[index[i]].append(scores[i])
        for idx in id2score:
            if len(id2score[idx]) == 1:
                id2mean[idx] = torch.tensor(0.0)
                id2std[idx] = torch.tensor(1.0)
            elif len(id2score[idx]) > 1:
                id2mean[idx] = torch.mean(torch.tensor(id2score[idx]))
                id2std[idx] = torch.std(torch.tensor([id2score[idx]]))
            else:
                raise ValueError(f"no score in prompt index: {idx}")
        for i in range(bsz):
            if norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo:
                scores[i] = (scores[i] - id2mean[index[i]]) / (id2std[index[i]] + epsilon)
            else:
                scores[i] = scores[i] - id2mean[index[i]]
        scores = scores.unsqueeze(-1) * response_mask

    return scores, scores


@register_adv_est(AdvantageEstimator.GRPO_PASSK)  # or simply: @register_adv_est("grpo_passk")
def compute_grpo_passk_outcome_advantage(
    token_level_rewards: torch.Tensor,
    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
    index: np.ndarray,
    epsilon: float = 1e-6,
    norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo: bool = True,
    config: Optional[AlgoConfig] = None,
    **kwargs,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """
    Compute advantage for Pass@k using a GRPO-style outcome reward formulation.
    Only the best response per group gets a non-zero advantage: r_max - r_second_max.

    Implemented as described in https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.19595.

    Args:
        token_level_rewards: (bs, response_length)
        response_mask: (bs, response_length)
        index: (bs,) → group ID per sample
        epsilon: float for numerical stability
        config: (AlgoConfig) algorithm settings, which contains "norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo"

    Returns:
        advantages: (bs, response_length)
        returns: (bs, response_length)
    """
    assert config is not None
    # if True, normalize advantage by std within group
    norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo = config.get("norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo", True)
    scores = token_level_rewards.sum(dim=-1)  # (bs,)
    advantages = torch.zeros_like(scores)

    id2scores = defaultdict(list)
    id2indices = defaultdict(list)

    with torch.no_grad():
        bsz = scores.shape[0]
        for i in range(bsz):
            idx = index[i]
            id2scores[idx].append(scores[i])
            id2indices[idx].append(i)

        for idx in id2scores:
            rewards = torch.stack(id2scores[idx])  # (k,)
            if rewards.numel() < 2:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Pass@k requires at least 2 samples per group. Got {rewards.numel()} for group {idx}."
                )

def compute_rewards(token_level_scores, old_log_prob, ref_log_prob, kl_ratio):
    """Compute token-level rewards with KL penalty.

    Args:
        token_level_scores (torch.Tensor): Token-level reward scores.
        old_log_prob (torch.Tensor): Log probabilities from current policy.
        ref_log_prob (torch.Tensor): Log probabilities from reference policy.
        kl_ratio (float): KL penalty coefficient.

    Returns:
        torch.Tensor: Token-level rewards with KL penalty applied.
    """
    kl = old_log_prob - ref_log_prob
    return token_level_scores - kl * kl_ratio


def agg_loss(loss_mat: torch.Tensor, loss_mask: torch.Tensor, loss_agg_mode: str):
    """
    Aggregate the loss matrix into a scalar.

    Args:
        loss_mat: `(torch.Tensor)`:

        loss_mask: `(torch.Tensor)`:
            shape: (bs, response_length)
        loss_agg_mode: (str) choices:
            method to aggregate the loss matrix into a scalar.

        loss: `a scalar torch.Tensor`

    """
    if loss_agg_mode == "token-mean":
        loss = verl_F.masked_mean(loss_mat, loss_mask)
    elif loss_agg_mode == "seq-mean-token-sum":
        seq_losses = torch.sum(loss_mat * loss_mask, dim=-1)  # token-sum
        loss = torch.mean(seq_losses)  # seq-mean
    elif loss_agg_mode == "seq-mean-token-mean":

def compute_policy_loss(
    old_log_prob,
    rollout_log_prob,
    log_prob,
    advantages,
    response_mask,
    cliprange=None,
    cliprange_low=None,
    cliprange_high=None,
    clip_ratio_c=3.0,
    loss_agg_mode: str = "token-mean",
    algo: str = "PPO",
):
    """
    Compute the clipped policy objective and related metrics for PPO.

    Adapted from
    https://github.com/huggingface/trl/blob/main/trl/trainer/ppo_trainer.py#L1122

    Args:
        old_log_prob (torch.Tensor):
            Log-probabilities of actions under the old policy, shape (batch_size, response_length).
        log_prob (torch.Tensor):
            Log-probabilities of actions under the current policy, shape (batch_size, response_length).
        advantages (torch.Tensor):
            Advantage estimates for each action, shape (batch_size, response_length).
        response_mask (torch.Tensor):
            Mask indicating which tokens to include in the loss, shape (batch_size, response_length).
        cliprange (float, optional):
            Clipping parameter ε for standard PPO. See https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.06347.
            Defaults to None (must be provided).
        cliprange_low (float, optional):
            Lower clip range for dual-clip PPO. Defaults to same as `cliprange`.
        cliprange_high (float, optional):
            Upper clip range for dual-clip PPO. Defaults to same as `cliprange`.
        clip_ratio_c (float, optional):
            Lower bound of the ratio for dual-clip PPO. See https://arxiv.org/pdf/1912.09729.
            Defaults to 3.0.
        loss_agg_mode (str, optional):
            Aggregation mode for `agg_loss`. Defaults to "token-mean".
    """
    assert clip_ratio_c > 1.0, (
        "The lower bound of the clip_ratio_c for dual-clip PPO should be greater than 1.0,"
        + f" but get the value: {clip_ratio_c}."
    )

    negative_approx_kl = log_prob - old_log_prob
    # Clamp negative_approx_kl for stability
    negative_approx_kl = torch.clamp(negative_approx_kl, min=-20.0, max=20.0)
    ratio = torch.exp(negative_approx_kl)
    ppo_kl = verl_F.masked_mean(-negative_approx_kl, response_mask)

    pg_losses1 = -advantages * ratio
    if cliprange_low is None:
        cliprange_low = cliprange
    if cliprange_high is None:
        cliprange_high = cliprange
    pg_losses2 = -advantages * torch.clamp(
        ratio, 1 - cliprange_low, 1 + cliprange_high
    )  # - clip(ratio, 1-cliprange, 1+cliprange) * A
    clip_pg_losses1 = torch.maximum(
        pg_losses1, pg_losses2
    )  # max(-ratio * A, -clip(ratio, 1-cliprange, 1+cliprange) * A)
    pg_clipfrac = verl_F.masked_mean(torch.gt(pg_losses2, pg_losses1).float(), response_mask)

    # pg_losses3 = -advantages * clip_ratio_c
    # clip_pg_losses2 = torch.min(pg_losses3, clip_pg_losses1)
    # pg_clipfrac_lower = verl_F.masked_mean(
    #     torch.gt(clip_pg_losses1, pg_losses3) * (advantages < 0).float(), response_mask
    # )
    # pg_losses = torch.where(advantages < 0, clip_pg_losses2, clip_pg_losses1)

    if algo in ["PPO", "PPO-Token-TIS", "PPO-Seq-MIS", "PPO-Seq-TIS"]:
        log_seq_iw = (old_log_prob - rollout_log_prob) * response_mask
        log_seq_iw = log_seq_iw.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
        seq_iw = torch.exp(log_seq_iw.clamp(max=20.0)) # sequence importance weight
        seq_iw = seq_iw.detach()
        if algo == "PPO":
            pg_losses = clip_pg_losses1
        elif algo == "PPO-Token-TIS":
            safe_log_token_iw = old_log_prob - rollout_log_prob
            safe_log_token_iw = safe_log_token_iw.clamp(max=20.0)
            token_iw = torch.exp(safe_log_token_iw)
            pg_losses = clip_pg_losses1 * token_iw.clamp(max=clip_ratio_c)
        elif algo == "PPO-Seq-TIS":
            pg_losses = clip_pg_losses1 * seq_iw.clamp(max=clip_ratio_c)
        elif algo == "PPO-Seq-MIS":
            clip_mask = (seq_iw <= clip_ratio_c).float()
            pg_losses = clip_pg_losses1 * seq_iw * clip_mask
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid algo: {algo}")
        pg_loss = agg_loss(loss_mat=pg_losses, loss_mask=response_mask, loss_agg_mode=loss_agg_mode)

        pg_clipfrac_lower = verl_F.masked_mean(
            torch.gt(seq_iw, clip_ratio_c).float(), response_mask
        )
    elif algo in ["PG-Seq-IS", "PG-Seq-TIS", "PG-Seq-MIS"]:
        log_seq_iw = (log_prob - rollout_log_prob) * response_mask
        log_seq_iw = log_seq_iw.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
        seq_iw = torch.exp(log_seq_iw.clamp(max=20.0))  # sequence importance weight
        seq_iw = seq_iw.detach()
        prob = torch.exp(log_prob)
        if algo == "PG-Seq-IS":
            seq_iw_truncated = seq_iw * log_prob
        elif algo == "PG-Seq-TIS":
            seq_iw_truncated = seq_iw.clamp(max=clip_ratio_c) * log_prob
        elif algo == "PG-Seq-MIS":
            seq_iw_truncated = (seq_iw * prob / prob.detach()).clamp(max=clip_ratio_c)
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid algo: {algo}")
        pg_losses = - seq_iw_truncated * advantages
        pg_loss = agg_loss(loss_mat=pg_losses, loss_mask=response_mask, loss_agg_mode="seq-mean-token-sum-norm")

        pg_clipfrac = verl_F.masked_mean(
            torch.gt(seq_iw, clip_ratio_c).float(), response_mask

            torch.lt(seq_iw, 1 / clip_ratio_c).float(), response_mask
        )
    elif algo in ["Vanilla-GSPO"]:
        low, high = 1 - 3e-4, 1 + 4e-4
        log_seq_iw = (log_prob - old_log_prob) * response_mask
        log_seq_iw = log_seq_iw.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
        seq_len = response_mask.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)

        safe_log_seq_iw = log_seq_iw / seq_len
        safe_log_seq_iw = safe_log_seq_iw.clamp(max=20.0)
        geometric_seq_iw = torch.exp(safe_log_seq_iw)
        geometric_seq_iw = geometric_seq_iw.detach()
        prob = torch.exp(log_prob)
        seq_ratio = geometric_seq_iw * prob / prob.detach()
        pg_losses1 = -advantages * seq_ratio
        pg_losses2 = -advantages * torch.clamp(
            seq_ratio, low, high
        )  # - clip(ratio, 1-cliprange, 1+cliprange) * A

        pg_losses = torch.maximum(
            pg_losses1, pg_losses2
        )  # max(-ratio * A, -clip(ratio, 1-cliprange, 1+cliprange) * A)

        agg_mode = "seq-mean-token-mean"
        pg_loss = agg_loss(loss_mat=pg_losses, loss_mask=response_mask, loss_agg_mode=agg_mode)

        seq_iw = torch.exp(log_seq_iw)
        pg_clipfrac = verl_F.masked_mean(torch.gt(pg_losses2, pg_losses1).float(), response_mask)
        pg_clipfrac_lower = verl_F.masked_mean(
            torch.gt(seq_iw, clip_ratio_c).float(), response_mask
        )
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid algo: {algo}")

    return pg_loss, pg_clipfrac, ppo_kl, pg_clipfrac_lower

# Tokenizer class or path. If null, it will be inferred from the model.
tokenizer: null

# Whether to use shared memory for data loading.
use_shm: False

# Training set parquet. Can be a list or a single file.
# The program will read all files into memory, so it can't be too large (< 100GB).
# The path can be either a local path or an HDFS path.
# For HDFS path, we provide utils to download it to DRAM and convert it to a local path.
train_files: ~/data/rlhf/gsm8k/train.parquet

# Validation parquet. Can be a list or a single file.
val_files: ~/data/rlhf/gsm8k/test.parquet

# The field in the dataset where the prompt is located. Default is 'prompt'.
prompt_key: prompt

# The field used to select the reward function (if using different ones per example).
reward_fn_key: data_source

# Maximum prompt length. All prompts will be left-padded to this length.
# An error will be reported if the length is too long.
# oc.select: default val for rollout.prompt_length
max_prompt_length: 512

# Maximum response length. Rollout in RL algorithms (e.g. PPO) generates up to this length.
# oc.select: default val for rollout.response_length
max_response_length: 512

# Batch size sampled for one training iteration of different RL algorithms.
train_batch_size: 1024

# Batch size used during validation. Can be null.
val_batch_size: null

# Whether to return the original input_ids without adding chat template.
# This is used when the reward model's chat template differs from the policy.
# If using a model-based RM with different templates, this should be True.
return_raw_input_ids: False

# Whether to return the original chat (prompt) without applying chat template.
return_raw_chat: False

# Whether to return the full prompt with chat template.
return_full_prompt: False

# Whether to shuffle the data in the dataloader.
shuffle: True

# num dataloader workers
dataloader_num_workers: 8

# Whether to shuffle the validation set.
validation_shuffle: False

# Whether to filter overlong prompts.
filter_overlong_prompts: False

# Number of workers for filtering overlong prompts.
# For large-scale datasets, filtering can be time-consuming.
# Use multiprocessing to speed up. Default is 1.
filter_overlong_prompts_workers: 1

# Truncate the input_ids or prompt if they exceed max_prompt_length.
# Options: 'error', 'left', 'right', 'middle'. Default is 'error'.
truncation: error

# The field in the multi-modal dataset where the image is located. Default is 'images'.
image_key: images

# The field in the multi-modal dataset where the video is located.
video_key: videos

# If the remote tokenizer has a Python file, this flag determines whether to allow using it.
trust_remote_code: False

# Optional: specify a custom dataset class path and name if overriding default loading behavior.
custom_cls:

  # The path to the file containing your customized dataset class. If not specified, pre-implemented dataset will be used.
  path: null

  # The name of the dataset class within the specified file.
  name: null

# Whether to return multi-modal inputs in the dataset. Set to False if rollout generates new multi-modal inputs.
return_multi_modal_inputs: True

# settings related to data sampler
sampler:

  # the path to the module containing a curriculum class which implements the
  # AbstractSampler interface
  class_path: null

  # the name of the curriculum class like `MySampler`
  class_name: null

# Data generation configuration for augmenting the dataset.
datagen:

  # The path to the file containing your customized data generation class.
  # E.g. 'pkg://verl.experimental.dynamic_dataset.dynamicgen_dataset'
  path: null

  # The class name of the data generation class within the specified file.
  # E.g. 'MockDataGenerator'
  name: null

124	def normalize_final_answer(final_answer: str) -> str:
125	    """Normalize a final answer to a quantitative reasoning question.
126	
127	    Args:
128	        final_answer: The answer string to normalize
129

131	        Normalized answer string
132	    """
133	    final_answer = final_answer.split("=")[-1]
134	
135	    # Apply substitutions and removals
136	    for before, after in SUBSTITUTIONS:
137	        final_answer = final_answer.replace(before, after)
138	    for expr in REMOVED_EXPRESSIONS:
139	        final_answer = final_answer.replace(expr, "")
140	
141	    # Extract and normalize LaTeX math
142	    final_answer = re.sub(r"(.*?)(\$)(.*?)(\$)(.*)", "$\3$", final_answer)
143	    final_answer = re.sub(r"(\text\{)(.*?)(\})", "\2", final_answer)
144	    final_answer = re.sub(r"(\textbf\{)(.*?)(\})", "\2", final_answer)
145	    final_answer = re.sub(r"(\overline\{)(.*?)(\})", "\2", final_answer)
146	    final_answer = re.sub(r"(\boxed\{)(.*)(\})", "\2", final_answer)
147	
148	    # Normalize shorthand TeX:

165	def is_correct_minerva(
166	    solution_str: str, gt: str, gt_need_extract: bool = False, answer_pattern: str = r"(?i)Answer\s*:\s*([^
]+)"
167	) -> tuple[bool, str]:
168	    """Check if the solution is correct according to Minerva criteria.
169	
170	    Args:
171	        solution_str: The solution string to check
172	        gt: The ground truth answer
173	        gt_need_extract: Whether the ground truth needs extraction
174	        answer_pattern: Regex pattern to extract the answer
175	
176	    Returns:
177	        Tuple of (is_correct, normalized_prediction)
178	    """
179	    # Extract answer from solution
180	    match = re.findall(answer_pattern, solution_str)
181	    extracted_answer = match[-1] if match else "[INVALID]"
182	    pred = normalize_final_answer(extracted_answer)
183	
184	    # Process ground truth
185	    if gt_need_extract:
186	        gt = normalize_final_answer(remove_boxed(last_boxed_only_string(gt)))
187	    else:
188	        gt = normalize_final_answer(gt)
189	
190	    return (pred == gt), pred

193	def is_correct_strict_box(
194	    pred: str, gt: str, pause_tokens_index: Optional[list[int]] = None
195	) -> tuple[int, Optional[str]]:
196	    """Check if the prediction is correct using strict boxed answer criteria.
197	
198	    Args:
199	        pred: The prediction string
200	        gt: The ground truth answer
201	        pause_tokens_index: Indices of pause tokens
202	
203	    Returns:
204	        Tuple of (score, extracted_prediction)
205	    """
206	    # Extract the relevant part of the prediction
207	    if pause_tokens_index is not None:
208	        assert len(pause_tokens_index) == 4
209	        pred = pred[pause_tokens_index[-1] - 100 :]
210	    else:
211	        pred = pred[-100:]
212	
213	    # Extract and check the boxed answer
214	    boxed_pred = last_boxed_only_string(pred)
215	    extracted_pred = remove_boxed(boxed_pred) if boxed_pred is not None else None
216	
217	    return 1 if (extracted_pred == gt) else -1, extracted_pred

220	def verify(
221	    solution_str: str, answer: str, strict_box_verify: bool = False, pause_tokens_index: Optional[list[int]] = None
222	) -> bool:
223	    """Verify if the solution is correct.
224	
225	    Args:
226	        solution_str: The solution string to verify
227	        answer: The ground truth answer
228	        strict_box_verify: Whether to use strict box verification
229	        pause_tokens_index: Indices of pause tokens
230	
231	    Returns:
232	        True if the solution is correct, False otherwise
233	    """
234	    if strict_box_verify:
235	        correct, pred = is_correct_strict_box(solution_str, answer, pause_tokens_index)
236	        return correct == 1, pred
237	
238	    correct, pred = is_correct_minerva(solution_str, answer)
239	    return correct, pred
240

242	def compute_score(
243	    solution_str: str,
244	    ground_truth: str,
245	    strict_box_verify: bool = False,
246	    pause_tokens_index: Optional[list[int]] = None,
247	) -> float:
248	    """Compute the reward score for a solution.
249	
250	    Args:
251	        solution_str: The solution string
252	        ground_truth: The ground truth answer
253	        strict_box_verify: Whether to use strict box verification
254	        pause_tokens_index: Indices of pause tokens
255	
256	    Returns:
257	        Reward score (1.0 for correct, -1.0 for incorrect)
258	    """
259	    # Limit solution length for efficiency
260	    solution_str = solution_str[-300:]  # The longest answer in MATH-500 has 159 characters
261	
262	    # Verify the solution
263	    correct, pred = verify(solution_str, ground_truth, strict_box_verify, pause_tokens_index)
264	
265	    reward = 1.0 if correct else -1.0
266	    acc = correct
267	
268	    return {
269	        "score": reward,
270	        "acc": acc,
271	        "pred": pred,
272	    }

import re
from typing import Optional


def last_boxed_only_string(string: str) -> Optional[str]:
    """Extract the last LaTeX boxed expression from a string.

    Args:
        string: Input string containing LaTeX code

    Returns:
        The last boxed expression or None if not found
    """
    idx = string.rfind("\\boxed{")
    if idx < 0:
        return None

    i = idx
    right_brace_idx = None
    num_left_braces_open = 0

    while i < len(string):
        if string[i] == "{":
            num_left_braces_open += 1
        if string[i] == "}":
            num_left_braces_open -= 1
            if num_left_braces_open == 0:
                right_brace_idx = i
                break
        i += 1

    return string[idx : right_brace_idx + 1] if right_brace_idx is not None else None


def remove_boxed(s: str) -> str:
    """Remove the LaTeX boxed command from a string.

    Args:
        s: String with format "\\boxed{content}"

    Returns:
        The content inside the boxed command
    """
    left = "\\boxed{"
    assert s[: len(left)] == left, f"box error: {s}"
    assert s[-1] == "}", f"box error: {s}"
    return s[len(left) : -1]


# Constants for normalization
SUBSTITUTIONS = [
    ("an ", ""),
    ("a ", ""),
    (".$", "$"),
    ("\\$", ""),
    (r"\ ", ""),
    (" ", ""),
    ("mbox", "text"),
    (",\\text{and}", ","),
    ("\\text{and}", ","),
    ("\\text{m}", "\\text{}"),
]

REMOVED_EXPRESSIONS = [
    "square",
    "ways",
    "integers",
    "dollars",
    "mph",
    "inches",
    "hours",
    "km",
    "units",

    "childrentickets",
    "multiples",
    "\\text{s}",
    "\\text{.}",
    "\\text{\ns}",
    "\\text{}^2",
    "\\text{}^3",
    "\\text{\n}",
    "\\text{}",
    r"\mathrm{th}",
    r"^\circ",
    r"^{\circ}",
    r"\;",
    r",\!",
    "{,}",
    '"',
    "\\dots",
]


def normalize_final_answer(final_answer: str) -> str:
    """Normalize a final answer to a quantitative reasoning question.

    Args:
        final_answer: The answer string to normalize

    Returns:
        Normalized answer string
    """
    final_answer = final_answer.split("=")[-1]

    # Apply substitutions and removals
    for before, after in SUBSTITUTIONS:
        final_answer = final_answer.replace(before, after)
    for expr in REMOVED_EXPRESSIONS:
        final_answer = final_answer.replace(expr, "")

import re

def last_boxed_only_string(string: str) -> Optional[str]:
    """Extract the last LaTeX boxed expression from a string.

    Args:
        string: Input string containing LaTeX code

    Returns:
        The last boxed expression or None if not found
    """
    idx = string.rfind("\\boxed{")
    if idx < 0:
        return None

    i = idx
    right_brace_idx = None
    num_left_braces_open = 0

    while i < len(string):
        if string[i] == "{":
            num_left_braces_open += 1
        if string[i] == "}":
            num_left_braces_open -= 1
            if num_left_braces_open == 0:
                right_brace_idx = i
                break
        i += 1

    return string[idx : right_brace_idx + 1] if right_brace_idx is not None else None


def remove_boxed(s: str) -> str:
    """Remove the LaTeX boxed command from a string.

    Args:
        s: String with format "\\boxed{content}"

    Returns:
        The content inside the boxed command
    """
    left = "\\boxed{"
    assert s[: len(left)] == left, f"box error: {s}"
    assert s[-1] == "}", f"box error: {s}"
    return s[len(left) : -1]

247	def _strip_properly_formatted_commas(expr: str):
248	    # We want to be careful because we don't want to strip tuple commas
249	    p1 = re.compile("(\d)(,)(\d\d\d)($|\D)")
250	    while True:
251	        next_expr = p1.sub("\\1\\3\\4", expr)
252	        if next_expr == expr:

258	def _normalize(expr: str) -> str:
259	    """Normalize answer expressions."""
260	    if expr is None:
261	        return None
262	
263	    # Remove enclosing `\text{}`.
264	    m = re.search("^\\\\text\{(?P<text>.+?)\}$", expr)
265	    if m is not None:

268	    expr = expr.replace("\\%", "%")
269	    expr = expr.replace("\\$", "$")
270	    expr = expr.replace("$", "")
271	    expr = expr.replace("%", "")
272	    expr = expr.replace(" or ", " , ")
273	    expr = expr.replace(" and ", " , ")
274	
275	    expr = expr.replace("million", "*10^6")
276	    expr = expr.replace("billion", "*10^9")
277	    expr = expr.replace("trillion", "*10^12")
278	
279	    for unit in [

296	    ]:

298	    expr = re.sub(f"\^ *\\\\circ", "", expr)

340	    if count_unknown_letters_in_expr(expr) > 2:

354	def are_equal_under_sympy(ground_truth_normalized: str, given_normalized: str):
355	    are_equal = False
356	    try:
357	        expr = f"({ground_truth_normalized})-({given_normalized})"
358	        if should_allow_eval(expr):
359	            sympy_diff = _sympy_parse(expr)
360	            for arg in sympy_diff.args:
361	                if isinstance(arg, sympy.Integer) and len(str(arg.p)) > 100:
362	                    print(f"Bad sympy request, may hang. len {len(str(arg.p))}, expr {expr}")
363	                    return False
364	            simplified = sympy.simplify(sympy_diff)
365	            if simplified == 0:

372	def split_tuple(expr: str):
373	    """
374	    Split the elements in a tuple/interval, while handling well-formatted commas in large numbers
375	    """
376	    expr = _strip_properly_formatted_commas(expr)
377	    if len(expr) == 0:
378	        return []
379	    if (
380	        len(expr) > 2
381	        and expr[0] in TUPLE_CHARS
382	        and expr[-1] in TUPLE_CHARS
383	        and all([ch not in expr[1:-1] for ch in TUPLE_CHARS])
384	    ):
385	        elems = [elem.strip() for elem in expr[1:-1].split(",")]
386	    else:
387	        elems = [expr]

391	def last_boxed_only_string(string):
392	    idx = string.rfind("\\boxed")
393	    if idx < 0:
394	        idx = string.rfind("\\fbox")
395	        if idx < 0:
396	            return None
397	
398	    i = idx
399	    right_brace_idx = None
400	    num_left_braces_open = 0
401	    while i < len(string):
402	        if string[i] == "{":
403	            num_left_braces_open += 1
404	        if string[i] == "}":
405	            num_left_braces_open -= 1
406	            if num_left_braces_open == 0:
407	                right_brace_idx = i
408	                break
409	        i += 1
410	    
411	    if right_brace_idx == None:
412	        retval = None
413	    else:
414	        retval = string[idx:right_brace_idx + 1]
415	    
416	    return retval

418	def remove_boxed(s):
419	    left = "\\boxed{"
420	    try:
421	        assert s[:len(left)] == left
422	        assert s[-1] == "}"
423	        return s[len(left):-1]
424	    except:
425	        return None
426

428	def extract_boxed_answer(solution: str) -> str:
429	    """Extract the answer from inside a LaTeX \\boxed{} command"""
430	    solution = last_boxed_only_string(solution)
431	    solution = remove_boxed(solution)
432	    return solution
433	
434	def grade_answer_sympy(given_answer: str, ground_truth: str) -> bool:
435	    ground_truth_normalized = _normalize(ground_truth)
436	    given_normalized = _normalize(given_answer)
437	
438	    if ground_truth_normalized is None:
439	        return False
440	
441	    if ground_truth_normalized == given_normalized:
442	        return True
443	
444	    if len(given_normalized) == 0:
445	        return False
446	
447	    ground_truth_elems = split_tuple(ground_truth_normalized)
448	    given_elems = split_tuple(given_normalized)
449	
450	    if len(ground_truth_elems) > 1 and (
451	        ground_truth_normalized[0] != given_normalized[0]
452	        or ground_truth_normalized[-1] != given_normalized[-1]
453	    ):
454	        is_correct = False
455	    elif len(ground_truth_elems) != len(given_elems):
456	        is_correct = False
457	    else:
458	        for ground_truth_elem, given_elem in zip(ground_truth_elems, given_elems):
459	            if _is_frac(ground_truth_elem) and _is_frac(given_elem):
460	                # if fractions aren't reduced, then shouldn't be marked as correct
461	                # so, we don't want to allow sympy.simplify in this case
462	                is_correct = ground_truth_elem == given_elem
463	            elif _str_is_int(ground_truth_elem) != _str_is_int(given_elem):
464	                # if the ground truth answer is an integer, we require the given answer to be a strict match (no sympy.simplify)
465	                is_correct = False
466	            else:
467	                is_correct = are_equal_under_sympy(ground_truth_elem, given_elem)
468	            if not is_correct:
469	                break
470	
471	    return is_correct
472	
473	def grade_answer_mathd(given_answer: str, ground_truth: str) -> bool:
474	    ground_truth_normalized_mathd = mathd_normalize_answer(ground_truth)
475	    given_answer_normalized_mathd = mathd_normalize_answer(given_answer)
476	
477	    # be at least as lenient as mathd
478	    if ground_truth_normalized_mathd == given_answer_normalized_mathd:
479	        return True
480	    return False
481	
482	def extract_answer(passage: str) -> str:
483	    if "\\boxed" in passage:
484	        return extract_boxed_answer(passage)
485	    return None
486	
487	def grade_answer_verl(solution_str, ground_truth):
488	    if not ground_truth:
489	        return False
490	    if '\\boxed' in ground_truth:
491	        ground_truth = extract_answer(ground_truth)
492	    given_answer = extract_answer(solution_str)
493	    if given_answer is None:
494	        return False
495	    return grade_answer_mathd(given_answer, ground_truth) \
496	        or grade_answer_sympy(given_answer, ground_truth)

from collections import defaultdict

import torch

from verl import DataProto
from verl.utils.reward_score import default_compute_score
from verl.workers.reward_manager import register


@register("naive")
class NaiveRewardManager:
    """The reward manager."""

    def __init__(self, tokenizer, num_examine, compute_score=None, reward_fn_key="data_source") -> None:
        """
        Initialize the NaiveRewardManager instance.

        Args:
            tokenizer: The tokenizer used to decode token IDs into text.
            num_examine: The number of batches of decoded responses to print to the console for debugging purpose.
            compute_score: A function to compute the reward score. If None, `default_compute_score` will be used.
            reward_fn_key: The key used to access the data source in the non-tensor batch data. Defaults to
                "data_source".
        """
        self.tokenizer = tokenizer  # Store the tokenizer for decoding token IDs
        self.num_examine = num_examine  # the number of batches of decoded responses to print to the console
        self.compute_score = compute_score or default_compute_score
        self.reward_fn_key = reward_fn_key  # Store the key for accessing the data source

    def __call__(self, data: DataProto, return_dict=False):
        """We will expand this function gradually based on the available datasets"""

        # If there is rm score, we directly return rm score. Otherwise, we compute via rm_score_fn
        if "rm_scores" in data.batch.keys():
            if return_dict:
                return {"reward_tensor": data.batch["rm_scores"]}
            else:
                return data.batch["rm_scores"]

        reward_tensor = torch.zeros_like(data.batch["responses"], dtype=torch.float32)
        reward_extra_info = defaultdict(list)

        already_print_data_sources = {}

        for i in range(len(data)):
            data_item = data[i]  # DataProtoItem

            prompt_ids = data_item.batch["prompts"]

            prompt_length = prompt_ids.shape[-1]

            valid_prompt_length = data_item.batch["attention_mask"][:prompt_length].sum()
            valid_prompt_ids = prompt_ids[-valid_prompt_length:]

            response_ids = data_item.batch["responses"]
            valid_response_length = data_item.batch["attention_mask"][prompt_length:].sum()
            valid_response_ids = response_ids[:valid_response_length]

            # decode
            prompt_str = self.tokenizer.decode(valid_prompt_ids, skip_special_tokens=True)
            response_str = self.tokenizer.decode(valid_response_ids, skip_special_tokens=True)

            ground_truth = data_item.non_tensor_batch["reward_model"]["ground_truth"]
            data_source = data_item.non_tensor_batch[self.reward_fn_key]
            extra_info = data_item.non_tensor_batch.get("extra_info", {})
            num_turns = data_item.non_tensor_batch.get("__num_turns__", None)
            extra_info["num_turns"] = num_turns

            score = self.compute_score(
                data_source=data_source,
                solution_str=response_str,
                ground_truth=ground_truth,
                extra_info=extra_info,
            )

            if isinstance(score, dict):
                reward = score["score"]
                # Store the information including original reward
                for key, value in score.items():
                    reward_extra_info[key].append(value)
            else:
                reward = score

            reward_tensor[i, valid_response_length - 1] = reward

            if data_source not in already_print_data_sources:
                already_print_data_sources[data_source] = 0

            if already_print_data_sources[data_source] < self.num_examine:
                already_print_data_sources[data_source] += 1
                print("[prompt]", prompt_str)
                print("[response]", response_str)
                print("[ground_truth]", ground_truth)
                if isinstance(score, dict):
                    for key, value in score.items():
                        print(f"[{key}]", value)
                else:
                    print("[score]", score)

        if return_dict:
            return {
                "reward_tensor": reward_tensor,
                "reward_extra_info": reward_extra_info,
            }
        else:
            return reward_tensor

# Format checks enforced on CI:
# 1. Comments must appear above each field.
# 2. There must be a blank line between each field.
# 3. Inline comments (after a field on the same line) are not allowed.
# 4. Indentation level is respected for nested fields.

# specify the default per-component configs
defaults:

  # <folder_name>@<field_name>.<field_name>: <yaml_file_name>
  # actor_rollout_ref.actor: trainer/config/actor/dp_actor.yaml
  - actor@actor_rollout_ref.actor: dp_actor

  # trainer.npu_profile: trainer/config/npu_profile/npu_profile.yaml
  - npu_profile@trainer.npu_profile: npu_profile

  # data: trainer/config/data/legacy_data.yaml
  - data@data: legacy_data

  # Reference model config.
  # Reference model will be enabled when actor.use_kl_loss or/and algorithm.use_kl_in_reward is/are True.
  - ref@actor_rollout_ref.ref: dp_ref

  # Rollout model config.
  - rollout@actor_rollout_ref.rollout: rollout

  # Critic model config.
  - critic@critic: dp_critic

  # Reward model config.
  - reward_model@reward_model: dp_reward_model

  # load the reference default config, then apply the fields in the current yaml
  # self config override anything above
  - _self_

# config for actor, rollout and reference model
actor_rollout_ref:

  # Whether it's a hybrid engine, currently only supports hybrid engine
  hybrid_engine: true

  # common configs for the model
  model:

    # Huggingface model path. This can be either local path or HDFS path.
    path: ~/models/deepseek-llm-7b-chat

    # Custom chat template for the model.
    custom_chat_template: null

    # Whether to use shared memory (SHM) for accelerating the loading of model weights
    use_shm: false

    # Additional Python packages to register huggingface models/tokenizers.
    external_lib: null

    # Used to override model's original configurations, mainly dropout
    override_config: {}

    # Enable gradient checkpointing for actor
    enable_gradient_checkpointing: true

    # Enable activation offloading for actor
    enable_activation_offload: false

    # Whether to remove padding tokens in inputs during training
    use_remove_padding: false

    # Set to positive value to enable LoRA (e.g., 32)
    lora_rank: 0

    # LoRA scaling factor
    lora_alpha: 16

    # Target modules to apply LoRA. Options: "all-linear" (not recommended for VLMs) or
    # [q_proj,k_proj,v_proj,o_proj,gate_proj,up_proj,down_proj]
    target_modules: all-linear

    # Exclude modules from applying Lora. Similar usage to target_modules and Peft.
    # Example: '.*visual.*' for excluding the ViT in Qwen2.5-VL, as currently vllm does not support ViT Lora.
    exclude_modules: null

    # Whether to use Liger for linear layer fusion
    use_liger: false

53	class DataParallelPPOActor(BasePPOActor):
54	    def __init__(self, config, actor_module: nn.Module, actor_optimizer: torch.optim.Optimizer = None):
55	        """When optimizer is None, it is Reference Policy"""
56	        super().__init__(config)
57	        self.actor_module = actor_module
58	        self.actor_optimizer = actor_optimizer
59	
60	        self.use_remove_padding = self.config.get("use_remove_padding", False)
61	        if torch.distributed.get_rank() == 0:
62	            print(f"Actor use_remove_padding={self.use_remove_padding}")
63	        self.use_fused_kernels = self.config.get("use_fused_kernels", False)
64	        if torch.distributed.get_rank() == 0:
65	            print(f"Actor use_fused_kernels={self.use_fused_kernels}")
66	
67	        self.ulysses_sequence_parallel_size = self.config.ulysses_sequence_parallel_size
68	        self.use_ulysses_sp = self.ulysses_sequence_parallel_size > 1
69	
70	        if self.config.entropy_from_logits_with_chunking:
71	            entropy_from_logits = verl_F.entropy_from_logits_with_chunking
72	        else:
73	            entropy_from_logits = verl_F.entropy_from_logits
74	
75	        self.compute_entropy_from_logits = (
76	            torch.compile(entropy_from_logits, dynamic=True)
77	            if self.config.get("use_torch_compile", True)  #  use torch compile by default
78	            else entropy_from_logits
79	        )
80	        self.device_name = get_device_name()
81	        assert self.config.dtype in ["float16", "float32", "bfloat16"]
82	        if self.config.dtype == "float16":
83	            self.scaler = ShardedGradScaler(growth_interval=400)
84	        else:
85	            self.scaler = None

87	    def _forward_micro_batch(
88	        self, micro_batch, temperature, calculate_entropy=False
89	    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
90	        """
91	        Returns:
92	            entropy: # (bs, response_len)
93	            log_probs: # (bs, response_len)
94	        """
95	        response_length = micro_batch["responses"].size(-1)
96	        multi_modal_inputs = {}
97	        if "multi_modal_inputs" in micro_batch.keys():
98	            if "image_bound" in micro_batch["multi_modal_inputs"][0]:  # minicpm-o logic
99	                for key in micro_batch["multi_modal_inputs"][0].keys():
100	                    multi_modal_inputs[key] = [inputs[key] for inputs in micro_batch["multi_modal_inputs"]]
101	            else:
102	                for key in micro_batch["multi_modal_inputs"][0].keys():
103	                    multi_modal_inputs[key] = torch.cat(
104	                        [inputs[key] for inputs in micro_batch["multi_modal_inputs"]], dim=0
105	                    )
106	
107	        from verl.utils.torch_dtypes import PrecisionType
108	        torch_dtype = PrecisionType.to_dtype(self.config.dtype)
109	        with torch.autocast(device_type=self.device_name, dtype=torch_dtype):
110	        # with nullcontext():
111	            input_ids = micro_batch["input_ids"]
112	            batch_size, seqlen = input_ids.shape
113	            attention_mask = micro_batch["attention_mask"]
114	            position_ids = micro_batch["position_ids"]
115	            entropy = None
116	            if position_ids.dim() == 3:  # qwen2vl mrope
117	                position_ids = position_ids.transpose(0, 1)  # (bsz, 3, seqlen) -> (3, bsz, seqlen)
118	
119	            if self.use_remove_padding:
120	                input_ids_rmpad, indices, cu_seqlens, *_ = unpad_input(
121	                    input_ids.unsqueeze(-1), attention_mask
122	                )  # input_ids_rmpad (total_nnz, ...)
123	                input_ids_rmpad = input_ids_rmpad.transpose(0, 1)  # (1, total_nnz)
124	
125	                # unpad the position_ids to align the rotary
126	                if position_ids.dim() == 3:
127	                    position_ids_rmpad = (
128	                        index_first_axis(rearrange(position_ids, "c b s ... -> (b s) c ..."), indices)
129	                        .transpose(0, 1)
130	                        .unsqueeze(1)
131	                    )  # (3, bsz, seqlen) -> (3, 1, bsz * seqlen)
132	                else:
133	                    position_ids_rmpad = index_first_axis(
134	                        rearrange(position_ids.unsqueeze(-1), "b s ... -> (b s) ..."), indices
135	                    ).transpose(0, 1)
136	
137	                if "image_bound" in multi_modal_inputs:
138	                    from verl.utils.dataset.vision_utils import process_multi_modal_inputs_for_minicpmo
139	
140	                    multi_modal_inputs = process_multi_modal_inputs_for_minicpmo(
141	                        input_ids, attention_mask, position_ids, cu_seqlens, multi_modal_inputs
142	                    )
143	
144	                # for compute the log_prob
145	                input_ids_rmpad_rolled = torch.roll(input_ids_rmpad, shifts=-1, dims=1)  # (1, total_nnz)
146	
147	                # pad and slice the inputs if sp > 1
148	                if self.use_ulysses_sp:
149	                    is_vlm_model = "multi_modal_inputs" in micro_batch.keys()
150	                    if is_vlm_model:
151	                        # vlm model's inputs will be sliced after embedding
152	                        input_ids_rmpad, position_ids_rmpad, pad_size = ulysses_pad(
153	                            input_ids_rmpad,
154	                            position_ids_rmpad=position_ids_rmpad,
155	                            sp_size=self.ulysses_sequence_parallel_size,
156	                        )
157	                    else:
158	                        input_ids_rmpad, position_ids_rmpad, pad_size = ulysses_pad_and_slice_inputs(
159	                            input_ids_rmpad,
160	                            position_ids_rmpad=position_ids_rmpad,
161	                            sp_size=self.ulysses_sequence_parallel_size,
162	                        )
163	                    input_ids_rmpad_rolled, _, _ = ulysses_pad_and_slice_inputs(
164	                        input_ids_rmpad_rolled,
165	                        position_ids_rmpad=None,
166	                        sp_size=self.ulysses_sequence_parallel_size,
167	                    )
168	
169	                input_ids_rmpad_rolled = input_ids_rmpad_rolled.squeeze(0)  # ((total_nnz / sp) + pad)
170	
171	                # only pass input_ids and position_ids to enable flash_attn_varlen
172	                extra_args = {}
173	                if self.use_fused_kernels:
174	                    extra_args["temperature"] = temperature
175	                    extra_args["return_dict"] = True
176	
177	                output = self.actor_module(
178	                    input_ids=input_ids_rmpad,
179	                    attention_mask=None,
180	                    position_ids=position_ids_rmpad,
181	                    **multi_modal_inputs,
182	                    use_cache=False,
183	                    **extra_args,
184	                )  # prevent model thinks we are generating
185	
186	                if self.use_fused_kernels:
187	                    log_probs = output.log_probs.squeeze(0)  # (total_nnz,)
188	                    entropy_rmpad = output.entropy.squeeze(0)  # (total_nnz,)
189	
190	                else:
191	                    logits_rmpad = output.logits.squeeze(0)  # (total_nnz, vocab_size)
192	                    logits_rmpad.div_(temperature)
193	
194	                    # if use_sp: ((total_nnz / sp) + pad) ; if not use_sp: (batch, seqlen)
195	                    inplace_backward = True
196	                    if calculate_entropy:
197	                        inplace_backward = False
198	                    log_probs = logprobs_from_logits(
199	                        logits=logits_rmpad,
200	                        labels=input_ids_rmpad_rolled,
201	                        inplace_backward=inplace_backward,
202	                    )
203	                    # print(f"logits dtype: {logits_rmpad.dtype}, log_probs dtype: {log_probs.dtype}")  # bf16, fp32
204	
205	                    # compute entropy
206	                    if calculate_entropy:
207	                        if not self.config.entropy_checkpointing:
208	                            entropy_rmpad = self.compute_entropy_from_logits(logits_rmpad)  # ((total_nnz / sp) + pad)
209	                        else:
210	                            entropy_rmpad = torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint(
211	                                self.compute_entropy_from_logits, logits_rmpad
212	                            )
213	
214	                # gather log_prob if sp > 1
215	                if self.use_ulysses_sp:
216	                    # gather and unpad for the ulysses sp
217	                    log_probs = gather_outputs_and_unpad(
218	                        log_probs,
219	                        gather_dim=0,
220	                        unpad_dim=0,
221	                        padding_size=pad_size,
222	                    )
223	                    if calculate_entropy:
224	                        entropy_rmpad = gather_outputs_and_unpad(
225	                            entropy_rmpad,
226	                            gather_dim=0,
227	                            unpad_dim=0,
228	                            padding_size=pad_size,
229	                        )
230	                # pad back to (bsz, seqlen)
231	                if calculate_entropy:
232	                    full_entropy = pad_input(
233	                        hidden_states=entropy_rmpad.unsqueeze(-1),
234	                        indices=indices,
235	                        batch=batch_size,
236	                        seqlen=seqlen,
237	                    )
238	                full_log_probs = pad_input(
239	                    hidden_states=log_probs.unsqueeze(-1),
240	                    indices=indices,
241	                    batch=batch_size,
242	                    seqlen=seqlen,
243	                )
244	
245	                # only return response part:
246	                if calculate_entropy:
247	                    entropy = full_entropy.squeeze(-1)[:, -response_length - 1 : -1]  # (bsz, response_length)
248	                log_probs = full_log_probs.squeeze(-1)[:, -response_length - 1 : -1]  # (bsz, response_length)
249	
250	            else:  # not using rmpad and no ulysses sp
251	                extra_args = {}
252	                if self.use_fused_kernels:
253	                    extra_args["temperature"] = temperature
254	                    extra_args["return_dict"] = True
255	
256	                output = self.actor_module(
257	                    input_ids=input_ids,
258	                    attention_mask=attention_mask,
259	                    position_ids=position_ids,
260	                    **multi_modal_inputs,
261	                    use_cache=False,
262	                    **extra_args,
263	                )  # prevent model thinks we are generating
264	
265	                if self.use_fused_kernels:
266	                    log_probs = output.log_probs[:, -response_length - 1 : -1]
267	                    entropy = output.entropy[:, -response_length - 1 : -1]  # (bsz, response_length)
268	
269	                else:
270	                    logits = output.logits
271	
272	                    logits.div_(temperature)
273	                    logits = logits[:, -response_length - 1 : -1, :]  # (bsz, response_length, vocab_size)
274	                    log_probs = logprobs_from_logits(logits, micro_batch["responses"])
275	                    if calculate_entropy:
276	                        if not self.config.entropy_checkpointing:
277	                            entropy = verl_F.entropy_from_logits(logits)  # (bsz, response_length)
278	                        else:
279	                            entropy = torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint(verl_F.entropy_from_logits, logits)
280	
281	            return entropy, log_probs
282	
283	    def _optimizer_step(self):
284	        assert self.config.grad_clip is not None
285	
286	        if self.scaler is not None:
287	            self.scaler.unscale_(self.actor_optimizer)
288	        if isinstance(self.actor_module, FSDP):
289	            grad_norm = self.actor_module.clip_grad_norm_(max_norm=self.config.grad_clip)
290	        elif isinstance(self.actor_module, FSDPModule):
291	            grad_norm = fsdp2_clip_grad_norm_(self.actor_module.parameters(), max_norm=self.config.grad_clip)
292	        else:
293	            grad_norm = torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(self.actor_module.parameters(), max_norm=self.config.grad_clip)
294	
295	        if self.scaler is not None:
296	            self.scaler.step(self.actor_optimizer)
297	            self.scaler.update()
298	        else:
299	            # if grad_norm is not finite, skip the update
300	            if not torch.isfinite(grad_norm):
301	                print(f"WARN: rank {torch.distributed.get_rank()} grad_norm is not finite: {grad_norm}")
302	                self.actor_optimizer.zero_grad()
303	            else:
304	                self.actor_optimizer.step()
305	
306	        from run_support import record_optimizer
307	        record_optimizer(self, grad_norm)
308	        return grad_norm
